name: Interactive applicant checks and early-employment identity continuity

attribution.legal_posture: This is official national-CERT prevention guidance based on a reported near miss; it is neither an independently investigated Thai incident nor a person attribution, legal finding, or adjudication.

caveats: The Register-derived account is a reported account; its Thai case status remains unadjudicated and independently unverified.
The anecdotal applicant stays an unnamed example rather than a named person or persona.
Facial appearance, accent, camera artifacts, nationality, AI use and remote work are contextual features; DPRK attribution requires source-backed corroboration.
A live video check supports liveness review; facial recognition and biometric matching are separate capabilities.
This record retains no person, company, account, address, identifier, image, payment selector, victim, or private data.
This is prevention or policy context; newly observed IT-worker incident and enforcement-result status are unreported.

statements: ThaiCERT's February 2026 item adds a newer Thai-language source for defending against fraudulent technical applicants. Its narrow delta is not the visual anomalies in the anecdote, but the control sequence: disable virtual backgrounds when appropriate, ask the applicant to perform a simple live interaction with a physical object, and use a lawful early-employment in-person or equivalent identity-continuity check for higher-risk roles.
AI-generated résumés and false professional profiles can be combined with deepfake video and real-time AI-assisted answers.
A live interaction challenge can supplement, but not replace, document, employment, device, network and behavioral verification.
Identity assurance should continue into early employment rather than ending at interview completion.
limitations: Official national-CERT prevention guidance based on a reported near miss; not an independently investigated Thai incident, person attribution, legal finding, or adjudication.
The February 2026 ThaiCERT guidance describes physical-object, virtual-background, and first-week checks; its repetition of threat patterns and Amazon totals is not independent corroboration.
Do not publish the anecdotal applicant as a named person or persona.
Do not treat facial appearance, accent, camera artifacts, nationality, AI use or remote work alone as DPRK indicators.
Do not turn a live video check into facial recognition or biometric matching.
Do not present the Register-derived account as an adjudicated or independently verified Thai case.
The physical-object and virtual-background checks are supplemental controls, not biometric matching, facial recognition, or standalone attribution signals.

sources.support: ThaiCERT's February 2026 item adds a newer Thai-language source for defending against fraudulent technical applicants. Its narrow delta is not the visual anomalies in the anecdote, but the control sequence: disable virtual backgrounds when appropriate, ask the applicant to perform a simple live interaction with a physical object, and use a lawful early-employment in-person or equivalent identity-continuity check for higher-risk roles. Original-language-source support (th): ThaiCERT describes an applicant believed to be part of a North Korean IT-worker scheme using a false LinkedIn profile, an AI-generated résumé, deepfake video and answers resembling material the interviewer had posted online. It recommends disabling virtual backgrounds, asking an applicant to interact with a physical object, and in some circumstances verifying a new hire in person during the first week. English translation note: Researcher translation from Thai. 'คาดว่าเป็นกลุ่มไอทีชาวเกาหลีเหนือ' is rendered as 'believed to be part of a North Korean IT-worker group,' not as a confirmed legal attribution
